# Private Research Entry Point: Source Dossier for Daily Digest (Issue 029)

This dossier contains the strongest cultural, technological, and archival signals compiled for Muki over the past 24 to 48 hours. The entries focus on feminist visual culture, photography, media archaeology, AI-native workflows, and East Asian contemporary art.

---

## 1. Visual Culture Signal

*   **Exact Title:** Skate of the Art: Skateboarding Across Cultures
*   **Proposed Section:** Visual Culture Signal / Photography & Exhibition
*   **Specific Source URL:** [Fotografiska Shanghai - Skate of the Art](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHKRUCh9HPolD_p5qfCWZOJjnY2R66I5mNXd1XKvjX_DpPKDwZWKDnnBatKr97Jyo-78svZGfeZYNJlMc48t-yXumghLqFtvUw2jxkTS5Bd1WibDNBj4S20_sOPQw25w_Wmjn3_-MUz6WsVECvkosk8sg6BVTWe)
*   **Publication / Opening Date:** July 24, 2026 (Runs through October 25, 2026)
*   **Verified Facts:** 
    *   **Venue:** Fotografiska Shanghai (127 Guangfu Road, Jing'an District, Shanghai).
    *   **Artists & Roster:** Features over 20 photographers, artists, and visual creators from five continents. Chinese artists include Bilal (比拉力), Songhui Rao (饶颂晖), Terry Xie (谢石), Yize Wan (万熠泽), and Zheng Zhou (周政). International artists include David Meskhi, Ed Templeton, Hugh Holland, Kenji Haruta, Larry Clark, Lauren Luxenberg, Luisa Dörr, Mike Blabac, Magdalena Wosinska, Marcel Veldman, Nikki Toole, Nils Svensson, Sem Rubio, TLB, Yassine Sellame, and Yoshiro Higai.
    *   **Format:** A major group exhibition deploying photography, video installations, multimedia elements, and raw street-textured elements.
    *   **Scope:** Traces the half-century evolution of skate culture from its roots in California (1970s) to its global and local contemporary manifestations, exploring how the camera lens has shaped and driven the subculture's development.
*   **Relevance to Muki:** This exhibition explores skateboarding as an anarchic practice, a lived attitude, and a physical code. It fits Muki's interest in vernacular visual cultures, alternative physical archives, and the use of lenses to construct and validate community-driven spaces.
*   **Duplication Assessment (Repetition Notes):** Completely new signal. Unlike the archival exhibitions in previous issues which focused on political or domestic environments, this show investigates physical subcultural geographies and street photography archives in an East Asian institutional context.

## 2. AI Research / Creative Tech Signal

*   **Exact Title:** EU AI Act Article 50: Transparency Obligations Take Effect
*   **Proposed Section:** AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
*   **Specific Source URL:** [Cloud Security Alliance AI Safety Initiative Report](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEg1vYVBy94uzDqR5XZyNBwQH5EfwzljJ3xXo5ncc3LvKynOk8gnpvMKCCpcue4B_pX09L02EnSVBbXoAwEGN_8f42eS-RtFm_WDsMZEcEXVhXgeij84tiM7WE8SExjjphTFdAVlplVGjNLBEJmlvohwwCzVO9B3oaXrbLgPgKKHvWCKaIMWZn-nEWWpJ4mCuEnIQjxr9ouSwYZ7QhukDx7Fc2a) / [BSA TechPost Analysis](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGl_JzDv93uiock6gEUz5YWIkzdZoRsWoupDYlVB1HYoXdYU8HtRfUQhvLU0kh-Q4fXsGQJS_0MN08h9dYkVclkea684S3GaWryBZEA7dIGozj3JBCPyGtqzMfdW8N2SHpljVUs4YaWpta_h-t7K00V5V_AglQRM0ZgRiQhHOlRpNecPd5GZa0u2QAjDEToFtVbM1BHTsoAPfAuV2k=)
*   **Publication / Enforcement Date:** August 2, 2026
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **Regulatory Status:** While the EU Digital Omnibus package delayed high-risk AI system obligations (Annex III) to December 2, 2027, the transparency and disclosure requirements under **Article 50** went into effect on schedule on **August 2, 2026**. Fines for non-compliance are up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover.
    *   **Mandatory Actions:** 
        1. Providers and deployers of conversational AI (chatbots, virtual assistants) must explicitly inform users they are interacting with AI.
        2. Providers of generative AI systems must mark synthetic outputs (images, audio, video) in a machine-readable format. 
        3. Grandfathering rule: Generative AI systems already on the market before August 2, 2026, have a extended runway until **December 2, 2026** to meet the machine-readable watermarking requirement.
        4. Anyone deploying AI to generate or edit deepfakes or realistic synthetic media must visibly disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated.
    *   **Technical Context:** Voluntary icon sets for labeling have been released. However, independent security research from 2026 shows that watermarking schemes can be defeated at low cost, including public tools that bypass advanced detection protocols.
*   **Relevance to Muki:** Directly maps to Muki's interest in media power, image histories, and information integrity. This is not just a legal development but a major infrastructural change in how AI creative workflows must handle metadata, watermarking, and public trust.
*   **Duplication Assessment (Repetition Notes):** Completely new signal. Directly follows up on our ongoing tracking of metadata and structural trust (e.g., Google Earth spatial AI rollback on Aug 4).

## 3. Feminist Structure Signal

*   **Exact Title:** Lesbian life of photographer who fled Nazi Germany finally brought into focus / Discovering Lisel Haas
*   **Proposed Section:** Feminist Structure Signal / Archival Research
*   **Specific Source URL:** [Library of Birmingham - News Release](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQH0w_2-XECTMROHXT0YI0NWs4yuSM--u3dySOUm3dFmcdJDYFtG9cndNk2s9sOK5WhOprHJm0JmEOXb2Y4_ypz4FkXDY-ZQk7zq03OmDAssHxExg8TNHjiQtAQhE7a9IBpsvS-BY44MC8zurz8sgqc6tl7J7fNOMwQUi-RRpWWrQhflfwd-dfCFsOzG2eW9gnvjOm6_6pxz3XFHv16eprg=) / [Bertz Associates Project Page](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQH0RqLa0WgrUVKRHdDplScf0-zS6KC8JLp0oSPguWjjOog5PKZqk66XvlQgR2bOoVpZm9Dscn7sBFtB4FmGoCSHCiCRG4HIvIopTR3UivpqSxZmHSkSutDxetz_E_SVO19evb4BCWYuJUg=)
*   **Publication / Opening Date:** July 27, 2026 (Runs through December 12, 2026)
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **Subject:** German-Jewish photographer Lisel Haas (1898–1989) and her business/life partner Grete Bermbach. Haas established her own studio in Germany in 1928, fleeing to Birmingham after Kristallnacht in November 1938. Grete joined her in 1939.
    *   **Archive:** Comprises 258 boxes of photographs, letters, invoices, lecture notes, and retouching tools housed in the Library of Birmingham. It was cataloged with support from a National Archives 'Archives Revealed' grant.
    *   **Exhibition Elements:** Features historical portraits, photojournalism, and theatre photography (she was official photographer for the Birmingham Repertory Theatre from 1940 to 1961). It introduces newly commissioned contemporary art responses from Anu Gamanagari, Gibson Kochanek Studio, George Eksts, Laura Chen, and Rebecca Orleans.
    *   **Feminist/Queer Focus:** Features a family memoir by Francesca Skelton (Bermbach's great-niece) explicitly detailing their romantic partnership and joint commercial studio ownership—narratives historically obscured by wartime displacement and institutional cataloging.
*   **Relevance to Muki:** Explores how female domestic partnership and collective labor became strategies for survival under exile. Illustrates the "care-work" of archiving, demonstrating how personal family memoirs can activate institutional collections to correct historical erasures.
*   **Duplication Assessment (Repetition Notes):** Completely new signal. Complements previous archival activations (such as Kathleen Cleaver on Aug 6 and Tessa Boffin on Aug 5) but introduces a unique focus on refugee histories, theater archives, and collaborative cataloging.

## 4. China / East Asia Signal

*   **Exact Title:** Text in the Room, Deferred (文字在房间里，被推迟)
*   **Proposed Section:** China / East Asia Signal
*   **Specific Source URL:** [gdm Taipei Exhibition Views](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHaMfTCdwDBKd9vG3LcI52qvpvlB92rdVP9hn6HEoZMoo3XneoiByH-5pDgz3ifgUpo1urXZaJEAFPhw6yzWzMVEqs58Ukz--Xvh7rsIxFZIBUJaDJZYJz0RfxA93Vo1jOzC1KvxQiV3oT24z0J8O6KD7qDE1i2A98-sW39jFj9kT8ZoqoFFboQaxHzya8=) / [Taiwan News Review](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQF7m3gFGCEXkz6NyNcVg0JjvBe0eqOtoOYM-lD7YOIdg8ju0gGEeZQq5o8sutQYfPS9gibF9BQ6p1Ufy_1x-eo3__HGyTBArdfUU5VVm8_YGHLzAADu2W1wfRZeAaVh6D7HzMs=)
*   **Publication / Opening Date:** July 9 – September 5, 2026
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **Venue:** Galerie du Monde (gdm Taipei, Ruiguang Road, Neihu District, Taipei).
    *   **Curator & Artists:** Curated by Wang Jing. Features six artists from Taiwan, Hong Kong, and China: Cai Guo Jie (蔡國傑), Liu Wei Wei (劉偉偉), Weng Io Wong (黃詠瑤), Wu Lao Bai (武老白), Xu Tan (徐坦), and Yuen Nga Chi (袁雅芝).
    *   **Theme & Setup:** Utilizes moving images and social practice to transform the gallery space into an "unfinished room" that reflects collective anxiety and structural fragmentation.
    *   **Key Artworks:** 
        *   **Xu Tan:** Video works documenting women's experiences and verbal narratives within deeply patriarchal rural environments in China.
        *   **Liu Weiwei:** A legal-art social experiment in which factory workers voted to determine the public release of their recorded workplace footage.
*   **Relevance to Muki:** Deepens the study of social-practice moving images in East Asia. It directly touches on labor structures, factory power dynamics, and the linguistic/visual representation of women in rural patriarchal systems, offering strong links to media power.
*   **Duplication Assessment (Repetition Notes):** Completely new signal. This group exhibition expands on contemporary conceptual and documentary media practices in the region, bridging political, labor, and gender issues without repeating the historical art-historical perspectives of the MMCA or Singapore National Gallery shows.

## 5. Archive / Long Read / Opportunity

*   **Exact Title:** CICA Museum International Exhibition: Photography Now 2027 Open Call
*   **Proposed Section:** Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
*   **Specific Source URL:** [CICA Museum Open Call - ArtDeadline](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG2rFu4VxTWSIoWUrI_YrS2LbtnlPp_o3sWze8j-iYRjLLyVnn2C48eqeP5ssHkibsZcZ3QZDoxCajX6jcM_mUrJd0_9VeEBIHmyUUjL7FdkUKTB_lEuQY=)
*   **Submission Deadline:** August 20, 2026
*   **Verified Facts:**
    *   **Organizer:** CICA Museum (Gimpo, Gyeonggi, South Korea).
    *   **Scope:** International open call for "Photography Now 2027." Welcomes works ranging from traditional and digital photography to experimental practices, including image manipulation and AI-generated photography.
    *   **Exhibition Plan:** April 7 – 25, 2027.
    *   **Installation Support:** Selected digital works can be printed on A3 (297 × 420 mm) foam poster board and installed directly by CICA curators and assistants, bypassing international physical shipping hurdles for digital/computational creators.
*   **Relevance to Muki:** Highly actionable and high-quality regional opportunity located in South Korea. The explicitly open attitude toward digital, manipulated, and AI-native photography fits Muki's technical workflow and artistic curation profiles.
*   **Duplication Assessment (Repetition Notes):** Completely new open call. Complements the historical and analytical focus of the other sections by offering a real, current opportunity to participate in contemporary experimental image production in East Asia.
